nodes.summary: Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 19.23 "Yes, such groups exist"; Leary and Minasyan (Theorem 2.14) construct polycyclic groups, which are finitely presented and soluble, of every torsion length `n ≥ 1`, in particular of torsion length `3`. Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved…
nodes.title: Finitely presented soluble groups of torsion length greater than two

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finitely presented soluble group $G$ of torsion length greater than $2$, that is, such that $G / \mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is not torsion-free, where $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is the second term of the torsion series of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.23 (Chiodo–Vyas), finitely presented form

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has torsion length greater than $2$ when $G / \mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is not torsion-free, where $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is the second term of the torsion series of $G$: some element $g \in G$ outside $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ has a power $g^n$ with $n > 0$ in $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$.
nodes.title: Torsion length greater than two

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the torsion series of Chiodo and Vyas is the sequence of subgroups $\mathrm{Tor}_i(G)$ of $G$ defined by $\mathrm{Tor}_0(G) = 1$, the trivial subgroup, and, for each $i$, $\mathrm{Tor}_{i+1}(G)$ is the normal closure in $G$ of the set of elements $g$ such that $g^n \in \mathrm{Tor}_i(G)$ for some integer $n > 0$.
